qt: to the Council Sophia in 't Veld (Renew) Subject:

On 16 February 2024, a Chinese-Hungarian law enforcement summit was held in Budapest, where China’s Minister of Public Security, Wang Xiaohong, and the Hungarian Interior Minister, Sándor Pintér, signed agreements on strengthening law enforcement cooperation and joint patrols.1 Earlier, China concluded a similar agreement with Serbia, an EU candidate country, where Chinese police officers are now patrolling areas popular with Chinese businesses or tourists.2 1.
Has the Hungarian Government informed the Council about this cooperation and, if so, can the Council provide details?

Does the Council agree that these planned Chinese-Hungarian law enforcement cooperation and joint patrols in EU territory pose an enormous threat to democracy, public security and EU law enforcement cooperation?
Will the Council raise this matter during the Belgian Presidency, with a view to issuing a statement condemning this cooperation?
